findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Returned live mapping loses observed spend after native capture/recovery exhaustion and owner replacement
findings.smallest_reproduction: S1/matched.py, recursionlimit150 depths144/145: save ledger checkpoint; dispatch and settle once; call pinned through native deep stack; raw tuple survives in _uncompared; replace registry ledger by checkpoint; dispatch original admitted action.
findings.actual_result: Live mapping: calls2, redispatch_refused false, pending raw tuple, unread empty. Same depths with owner-published dict copies: calls1, redispatch_refused true, seal None.
findings.expected_result: Previously handed spend cannot disappear into authoritative equality after interrupted capture; honest readers remain recoverable.
findings.trust_boundary: Native BudgetLedger settlement and public checkpoint restoration through owner registry. RecursionError is native; no private owner mutation, production monkeypatch, sleeps, or forged evidence. Diagnostics inspect private reader fields but do not write them.
findings.proposed_correction: Decide stable owner publication lifetime; detached mapping membership plus preserved original account histories is sufficient for demonstrated replacement. Then add bounded no-lost-handing and honest recovery controls. Do not mandate acknowledgement subsystem from this reproduction.

repair_assessment.json_parity: CONFIRMED in bounded controls: 32 R16/R17 tests passed, including numeric-key/sequence detached equivalence, owner order/default=str, genuine rollback/rewrite refusal and invalid-owner unresolved barriers. Static comparison confirms _retained_entry follows each owner write/read ordering, and complete-account checks remain in _read_once.
repair_assessment.seal: Existing R16 concurrency controls executed; changed helper still resolves outside lock and exact barrier/seal checks remain. No new seal bypass established.
repair_assessment.documentation: Current class explicitly calls pre-capture loss unresolved; no accepted stack exclusion.

minimum_correction_assessment.concrete_blocker: After both retention attempts fail, only raw live registry survives. Registry replacement destroys its old binding. A later reader now sees the same state as an unchanged honest callback trace; no generic later normalization or retry can infer whether erased spend existed. This is a concrete lost-information boundary, not a universal impossibility theorem.
minimum_correction_assessment.reader_only: Additional retries, moving dict copy earlier, fresh-stack capture, or catching narrower failures can fix bounded schedules and may be useful local improvements. None demonstrated preservation across repeated failure before capture under unchanged arbitrary mutable-return contract. A permanent unresolved marker prevents redispatch but can permanently poison an honest reader without corruption, violating the second requirement. A bounded timeout that later accepts has no lost information to justify acceptance.
minimum_correction_assessment.minimum_owner_decision: Execution owner publishes a new dictionary pair whose ID-to-account bindings remain stable while referenced by reader; checkpoint replacement changes only current registry. Existing native account records remain the authority. Callback signature may stay identical, but stable publication/lifetime is an added semantic obligation and is not silently assumed.
minimum_correction_assessment.wrapper_limit: A generic reader wrapper calling the old arbitrary callback then copying its returned maps has a post-inner-return/pre-copy window. This is not equivalent to owner-produced detached publication. A bounded recursion-depth workaround is not evidence of all-interruption preservation.
minimum_correction_assessment.acknowledgement: Explicit acknowledgement may bound retention or support more mutable owners, but is not established necessary. Python reference lifetime can preserve detached dictionaries for this demonstrated replacement. C1 defect confirmed; any claim that full acknowledgement is mandatory is not supported by controls.
minimum_correction_assessment.nested_state: Shallow copies preserve binding only. Append-only old histories survive replacement; arbitrary in-place mutation/rewrite of referenced accounts or entry payloads needs scoped trust/lifetime semantics or stronger owner snapshot. Do not conflate shallow map stability with entire graph immutability.
minimum_correction_assessment.limits: No implementation or approval of owner contract. Whole arbitrary asynchronous-interruption and pre-registration proof absent. Current controls show a viable bounded correction, not closure.
